subject: Invoice delivery: signed/PDF fingerprint and sender identity
thread_summary: Customer asks whether Redwood can provide a signed invoice fingerprint (PDF hash) and enforce sender identity headers for emailed invoices; internal ops clarifies portal vs email fallback, SFTP file naming, and required SPF/DKIM headers. Final decision: accept signed PDF with SHA256 fingerprint in email body + portal primary, email as temporary fallback.
messages:
From: Lara Chen <ap@blueflux.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Padgett <simon.padgett@blueflux.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice delivery and signature - file fingerprinting?

Hi Naomi,

Quick question from AP: for our audit we need either (a) invoices uploaded to a vendor portal where file checksums are preserved, or (b) emailed PDFs that include a verifiable fingerprint (SHA256) in the message body and a stable sender identity so our system can auto-ingest.

Can Redwood:
- Include a SHA256 hash of the final PDF in the invoice email body?
- Guarantee the sender is a fixed email (inbox) with SPF/DKIM alignment so our mail parser trusts it?
- Alternatively, can we pull invoices via SFTP with a predictable filename pattern and a delivery manifest?

We prefer portal push but need the email fallback for the first two billing cycles. Also need VAT tagging on each invoice line. Please let me know implementation details and any timeline.

Thanks,
Lara Chen
AP Manager | BlueFlux Energy

Attachment: sample-invoice-202605.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <ap@blueflux.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery and signature - file fingerprinting?

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, yes, and yes (with notes). Detail below plus two delivery options and recommended default.

Options we support:
1) Portal-first (recommended): Redwood portal hosts invoices; each uploaded PDF gets a stored SHA256 hash exposed in the invoice metadata and available via the UI/API. We can also send a notification email with the fingerprint in the body for your ingest.
2) Email fallback (temporary): we can send emailed PDFs with an SHA256 fingerprint included as a single-line header in the message body (e.g. Invoice-SHA256: <hash>) and we will ensure messages are sent from a consistent address invoices@redwood-inference.com with DKIM/SPF aligned. This is intended as a short-term fallback (we suggest 60 days) while you finish portal enrollment.

SFTP pull: we support SFTP pick-up with a manifest CSV; file naming convention we recommend: blueflux_INV_<YYYYMMDD>_<INVOICEID>.pdf. Connor can paste a spec below.

VAT: Kimberly will confirm that each line will include VAT tags and the invoice will carry the summary VAT fields you need.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly: confirm VAT line-item tagging and any specific fields your parser needs.
- Connor: share SFTP filename & manifest spec and the mailbox/sender info we will use for fallback emails.
- Lara: confirm whether you want immediate portal onboarding or to start with email fallback for two cycles.

Happy to set a quick 20-min call if useful.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

--
Naomi Feldman
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice delivery and signature - file fingerprinting? (SFTP spec + sender identity)

Hi Lara — adding the technical details for SFTP and the email fallback so your engineering/AP team can validate parsing rules.

SFTP manifest (CSV) columns we provide: filename, invoice_id, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), total_amount, currency, sha256_hash, vat_amount, remit_entity
Recommended filename pattern: blueflux_INV_20260520_INV12345.pdf
Example manifest row: blueflux_INV_20260520_INV12345.pdf,INV12345,2026-05-20,12500.00,USD,3b6d4f...c8a,200.00,Redwood US LLC

Email fallback behavior:
- From address: invoices@redwood-inference.com (static sender)
- Envelope FROM / Return-Path configured with SPF record we control; DKIM-signed headers.
- Email body will include a single-line checksum header right above attachments: Invoice-SHA256: 3b6d4f...c8a
- Subject format: [Invoice][BlueFlux] INV12345 2026-05-20
- Attachment filename will match the SFTP pattern for consistency.

Security note: if BlueFlux requires an HMAC or signed manifest, we can produce a signed manifest file (manifest.sig) with an RSA signature; let us know the verifier key you prefer.

I've attached a short CSV with filename guidelines.

Connor O'Brien
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
